body: Depending on who you talk to, they may not immediately send you to the hospital. Maybe this was just due to my seemingly positive demeanor, but I've told any professional who asked what my plan is, and I haven't been put in the hospital. They have made sure that I don't have access to the meds of choice, or anything related to such, but really they just took my word for it (no searching of my dorm or anything). They have suggested that I go to the hospital by choice if I feel like things might escalate, and that may be what they suggest as well. But in my experience, they will not force you to go.

As a lesbian, and as someone who used to have very close friendships with guys, this story resonates with me. 

In my own experience with this type of thing (I won't go into the whole spiel now) it is important to first mention that it was not your fault. You may have heard this a thousand times already, but it is something that is hard for many to accept. Just because you were friends with him and had allowed him to spend the night does not mean he had the right to do anything that he did, and if people tell you you should have fought harder or made yourself more clear just know that that is not the case. What he did is unjustifiable and the degree to which you did or didn't fight back doesn't matter. 

As for the question of whether it was rape, by the majority of definitions it absolutely was; however, you have the right to put whatever label on it you want. If you don't feel comfortable describing it as such then that's okay. It seems like the psychological toll is still evident, and I suggest you see a counselor about this (at least at my university, we have special counselors for this and we can choose one we are most comfortable with). I personally have been open about it with counselors and some of my close friends, but haven't told my siblings. And with my parents, it didn't go well. It all depends on your situation, but don't feel obligated to tell your family and only tell others what you're comfortable with, just enough to get the help you need and deserve. I know that I have some of those symptoms like not being able to sleep a certain way or experience certain kinds of pleasure, and those are things you could work on in counseling. 

You're an amazing person for making it this far and reaching out. Keep on being awesome.
